riskTone.label: BEARISH
riskTone.rationale: Iran escalating strikes on US bases signals geopolitical risk-off; higher-for-longer rate fears add hawkish headwind, both pressuring UK100.

briefing.briefing: GBP/USD is down 0.23% today, which — because of the inverse relationship between sterling and the FTSE 100 — is a mild tailwind for the index (a weaker pound makes the dollar and euro earnings of UK multinationals worth more in sterling terms), though the system rates the net FX impact as NEUTRAL given the small move and the Sterling ERI [a broad measure of the pound against a basket of currencies] barely shifting. The regime right now is a tug-of-war: the standout bullish force is Brent crude surging +5.79%, which directly lifts Shell and BP — the two biggest energy stocks in the index — and the ENERGY sector is flagged BULLISH; pulling the other way, US equities are soft (S&P 500 -0.65%, Nasdaq -1.66%), the VIX [a measure of expected market volatility, sometimes called the 'fear index'] sits at 17.28 in ELEVATED territory, and the broader risk tone is scored BEARISH. Banks are flagged BEARISH as 10-year gilt yields fell 6 basis points today, which slightly squeezes the profit margin banks earn on loans. Gilts are NOT in long-end stress, which removes one major worry. The key catalyst comes from Reuters roughly 7 hours ago: Iran escalating strikes on US bases — a classic geopolitical risk-off [investors moving away from riskier assets] headline that explains why the index gapped down 35 points from Friday's close and why safe-haven gold had already been bid before reversing (-2.97% today, suggesting some of that fear trade is unwinding). PHARMA (AstraZeneca) carries idiosyncratic risk — watch for any AZN-specific news that could independently swing the index. The directional bias is NEUTRAL to mildly bearish: the energy tailwind is real but not enough on its own to flip sentiment when geopolitical fear, soft US markets, and elevated VIX are all pressing down. Confidence is 4/10 — the Iran headline introduces unpredictable headline risk in either direction, and if tensions de-escalate, the index could bounce sharply; if they worsen, energy stocks won't save it. For the 08:00 ORB trade, 62% of the 14-day average daily range [the typical distance the index travels in a day, averaged over two weeks] has already been used up, the overnight range spans 10443 to 10526, and with a gap-down open and conflicting forces, today looks more like a fakeout/sweep-then-reverse day than a clean trend breakout — treat initial ORB breaks with scepticism and wait for a retest of the breakout level before committing. No scheduled UK data releases fall today; however, UK GDP Monthly Estimate at 07:00 BST on Wednesday (3 days away, HIGH impact) means conviction should be kept light as the week progresses and you should consider cutting position size ahead of that number. Key levels: ORB high 10526 and overnight high 10526.3 are essentially the same resistance; ORB low 10482 is the first downside pivot; prior day low 10438.8 is the line in the sand below that; prior close 10522.4 acts as the reference point for whether today's gap-down holds or fills. The one thing to remember today: Brent's surge keeps energy stocks fighting, but Iran headlines and a tired daily range make clean ORB trends unlikely — size down and wait for confirmation before trusting any break.
